newsitem.title: FINLAND: Russia insists it won good deal at summit.
newsitem.headline: Russia insists it won good deal at summit.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov insisted on Saturday Moscow had won a good deal at a U.S.-Russian summit, denying his country had been outflanked on NATO enlargement or bought off by the West.

Asked at a news conference whether Russia's bargaining position with the alliance had been weakened, Primakov said: "Russia stands by its negative position on NATO enlargement, and the agreement which we want to sign with NATO is not a pay-off for giving up that position.

"What happened yesterday was a real breakthrough...because we even reached agreement on those questions which, frankly speaking, we had earlier doubted could be agreed on," Primakov said after meeting Finnish Foreign Minister Tarja Halonen.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin agreed at the two-day summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton to sign a charter building a new relationship with NATO, despite Moscow's opposition to the eastward expansion of the alliance.

Yeltsin dropped a key Russian demand that the charter should be legally binding and also promised to minimise the differences over NATO enlargement, drawing charges from communist opponents in the Russian parliament (Duma) that Moscow had caved in to shameful defeat.

The summit agreement on NATO, Primakov said, would "make it more helpful for us to move towards signing the appropriate agreements". Decisions reached in Helsinki "coincide to a great degree with requirements voiced in the Duma", Primakov said.
